rounds.text: Apar Industries is fundamentally under-appreciated because its compounding execution significantly outpaces broad sector benchmarks, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 24% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 37% [E18, E21]. The underlying quality of the business is exceptionally high, evidenced by an outstanding ROCE of 27.5% and an ROE of 18.11%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 12.9% and 10.84% respectively [E9, E10]. Far from slowing down, the company is capturing massive structural global demand, highlighted by a towering conductor division pending order book of around INR10,190 crores—featuring a 56.8% export proportion—and massive new order inflows of INR5,245 crores in the quarter [E85, E86]. This growth engine is aggressively fueled by future capacity expansion, with capital expenditure planned to scale up to about INR1,500 crores for FY27 following INR740 crores incurred in FY26, alongside a massive 315.4% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 540 Cr [E41, E80]. Institutional confidence in this trajectory is underlined by positive institutional money flow with domestic holdings increasing to 24.88% [E44, E45]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 62.5x and a rich price-to-book of 13.41x, which leaves a negative margin of safety under standard DCF models [E1, E2, E47].

The valuation currently demanded by the market is fundamentally detached from the underlying cash flows and intrinsic value, as shown by a discounted cash flow model placing the intrinsic value at ₹11,511 against a market price of ₹18,005 [E46], leaving a stark negative margin of safety of -56.4% [E47]. This extreme pricing has pushed the price-to-earnings multiple to an elevated 62.5x [E1], which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 22.41x [E6], while the price-to-book ratio sits at 13.41x [E2] compared to its sector benchmark of 2.43x [E7]. Furthermore, expectations have aggressively outpaced operational delivery, with a reverse DCF revealing that today's price requires a steep 24.2% earnings growth rate just to justify itself, surpassing the base case projection of 18.0% [E48]. Operational vulnerabilities compound these valuation risks, highlighted by a notable -2.35 percentage point reduction in promoter holding down to 55.42% over recent quarters [E42], alongside rising borrowings that climbed to ₹956 crores from ₹585 crores a year earlier [E40]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing financial momentum with a 37% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21] and a high return on capital employed of 27.5% [E10]. Nevertheless, external shocks—such as volume contractions in the conductor division due to soaring metal prices [E89] and regional disruptions affecting the oil division [E90]—demonstrate the fragility of sustaining such high-priced expectations against cyclical volatility.

Conceded: [E46, E47] regarding the DCF intrinsic value calculation. However, the bear's emphasis on high valuation multiples like P/E of 62.5x [E1] and P/B of 13.41x [E2] ignores the company's superior return metrics, which feature an ROCE of 27.5% against a sector benchmark of 12.9% [E10] and an ROE of 18.11% versus a sector benchmark of 10.84% [E9]. Conceded: [E48] regarding the reverse DCF growth expectation. Yet, the reverse DCF demand is supported by actual delivery, shown by a 37% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21] and a 29% 5-year compounded sales growth [E15]. Regarding promoter holding dropping to 55.42% [E42], this is more than offset by strong institutional accumulation, with domestic institutions increasing their stake by 6.26 percentage points [E44] and total institutional money flow reading positive [E45]. Finally, while borrowings rose to ₹956 crores [E40], the debt-to-equity ratio remains at a conservative 0.18x [E38], and the temporary volume contractions [E89, E90] are countered by a robust conductor pending order book of ₹10,190 crores with 56.8% export proportion [E85].

Conceded: [E10, E9] regarding superior ROCE and ROE relative to sector benchmarks. However, the bull's reliance on past growth rates—such as 37% trailing profit growth [E21] and 29% five-year sales growth [E15]—to justify current multiples overlooks the severe price-led disconnect flagged by the signal engine, which notes price growth has exceeded profit growth by 75% [E58]. Conceded: [E44] regarding domestic institutional accumulation, but this does not invalidate the ongoing insider distribution evidenced by promoter holding declining to 55.42% [E42]. While the bull points to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E38], borrowings jumped sharply from ₹585 crores to ₹956 crores [E40], and the company is simultaneously ramping up capital expenditure to ₹1,500 crores for FY27 [E80] while facing volume contractions of 6.7% in conductors [E89] and 13.7% in oil [E90] due to external shocks. Finally, the massive pending order book in the conductor division [E85] fails to insulate earnings from operational friction, as evidenced by customers withholding manufacturing clearance due to surging metal prices [E89].

Conceded: [E58] regarding price growth outpacing profit growth, and [E42] regarding the minor reduction in promoter holding to 55.42%. However, the bear's alarm over rising borrowings to ₹956 crores [E40] ignores the conservatively managed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.18x [E38] and the robust operating cash flow of ₹968 crores [E35]. The massive jump in capital expenditure to ₹1,500 crores for FY27 [E80] is not a reckless risk but a direct response to structural tailwinds in energy infrastructure [E78], backed by a massive conductor pending order book of ₹10,190 crores with 56.8% in exports [E85]. While external shocks temporarily pressured volumes [E89, E90], absolute profitability expanded significantly, with conductor absolute EBITDA rising to ₹53,418 per ton from ₹43,688 [E84] and oil division EBITDA margins surging to ₹25,482 per kL from ₹7,004 [E83]. Finally, domestic institutions clearly recognize this underlying operational strength, aggressively increasing their stake by 6.26 percentage points to 24.88% [E44].

Conceded: [E35] regarding operating cash flow reaching Rs 968 Cr. However, the bull's dismissal of rising borrowings to Rs 956 Cr [E40] overlooks that borrowings have jumped from Rs 585 Cr a year earlier, representing a significant absolute debt expansion even against a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E38]. Furthermore, while the bull defends the aggressive FY27 capex plan of INR 1,500 crores [E80] as a response to infrastructure demand [E78], this massive capital expenditure follows a prior Rs 740 Cr spend [E80] and coincides with a sharp 315.4% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 540 Cr [E41], increasing execution risk before these projects generate returns. The bull's reliance on expanding absolute EBITDA per ton and per kL [E83, E84] ignores the operational vulnerabilities exposed during the quarter, including a 6.7% drop in conductor volumes and a 13.7% decline in oil volumes caused by metal price surges, geopolitical conflicts, and logistical bottlenecks [E89, E90]. Finally, while domestic institutions increased their holdings [E44], this was accompanied by a concurrent reduction in promoter stake to 55.42% [E42].

evidence.fact: Management stated that the structural energy infrastructure fundamentals remain robust, supported by growth in T&D, rising electricity demand, and increasing evacuation infrastructure.
evidence.quote: However, having said that, structurally, energy infrastructure fundamentals remain intact with the growth in T&D, rising electricity demand and evacuation infrastructure being increased, data center expansion, the growing presence of EVs, more opportunities for reconducting and upgradation of aging lines and, finally, the significant investment happening in ultra-high voltage transmission infrastructure and HVDC.

evidence.fact: Management noted that the Middle East business will remain somewhat subdued until the ongoing war is resolved.
evidence.quote: So I see that the Middle East business will continue to remain a little bit subdued until this war gets completed.

evidence.fact: The company plans to increase its capital expenditure for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores, following an expenditure of INR740 crores in FY26.
evidence.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.

evidence.fact: The planned capex breakup for FY27 includes around INR400 crores from the conductor division, around INR200-odd crores from the oil division, and approximately INR850 crores from the cable division.
evidence.quote: Around INR400 crores would be coming from conductor division, around INR200-odd crores on oil division, and cable would be in the range of INR850 crores.

evidence.fact: The company provided approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter in line with accounting standards due to sharp rises and falls in crude and gas oil prices.
evidence.quote: So, with the price of crude oil and gas oil having risen very sharply at the beginning of the quarter and then falling quite sharply at the end of the period, the company has followed the requirements of accounting standards and has provided for approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter.

evidence.fact: The oil division's EBITDA margins came in at a substantially higher level of INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 per kL a year ago.
evidence.quote: However, post taking this provision into account, the EBITDA margins came in at a substantially higher level of INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 per kL a year ago.

evidence.fact: Conductor division absolute EBITDA grew to INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.
evidence.quote: EBITDA growth is attributable to a higher share of the premium mix due to which despite a slightly lower volume of conventional conductors, the absolute EBITDA has grown, which came in at INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.

evidence.fact: The conductor division's pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%.
evidence.quote: The pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%.

evidence.fact: New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, with exports contributing 65.8%.
evidence.quote: New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, of which exports contributed to 65.8%.

evidence.fact: The cable division's pending order stands at INR1,925 crores compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.
evidence.quote: The pending order today stands at INR1,925 crores. So it largely covers the plan or the requirement for the current -- for the coming quarter compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.

evidence.fact: The quarter was challenging due to the impact of the U.S.-Iran war, logistics difficulties in export markets, and manpower shortages in May.
evidence.quote: Otherwise, this has been a fairly challenging quarter from an external perspective, given the impact of the U.S.-Iran war, various logistics difficulties that have happened in the export markets and fairly significant manpower-related shortages in the month of May, which coincided with holidays as well as local elections.

evidence.fact: Conductor volumes were down 6.7% due to a surge in metal prices impacting delivery schedules where customers withheld manufacturing clearance.
evidence.quote: Volume for the quarter was down 6.7% compared to a year ago. This can be attributed fundamentally to a surge in the metal prices that have impacted delivery schedules of orders which are in hand, where customers have withheld manufacturing clearance, especially due to the sudden increase in the price of aluminum and where customers were not having hedged metal.

evidence.fact: Oil division volumes were affected because the UAE facility was restricted to making local deliveries due to the crisis and resulting closure of the Hamriyah port.
evidence.quote: Volume for the quarter stands at 129,085 kL, down 13.7% compared to a year ago and down -- yes, the volumes were affected really because of our facility in the UAE, which because of this crisis and the resulting closure of the Hamriyah port was restricted to only making local deliveries of the product that it had in inventory.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): Large orders exceeding ₹ 2,800 crores from two major overseas electric utility companies have a delivery period spread over the next 4 years.
evidence.quote: This includes large orders exceeding ₹ 2,800 crores from two major overseas electric utility companies with a delivery period spread over next 4 years reinforcing the investments behind transmission capex globally

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Management stated that from a medium to long-term perspective, conductor margins are expected to be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton plus tailwinds.
evidence.quote: And based on the historical EBITDA margin that we have made, we expect that from a medium to long-term perspective, our conductor margins could be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company plans to increase its capital expenditure for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores.
evidence.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.
